bars.says: A crew reaches each sea floor and returns by gravship, lands clear of carrying water, and can work from the hull to the bank without using a hatch or a sea-surface settlement.

meant.intent: A playable expedition needs a return route and a safe arrival; refusing this is delegated from ship-or-nothing and the four-sea visit promise.
meant.source: Standing ship-only ruling, 2026-09-26 and 2026-10-01, biome_rulings.md; sea_surface_removal_2026-11-01.md; delegated safe-arrival inference from the current danger and sole return vehicle.

figurative.stands_for: Twilight channel cells whose dense current displaces unsecured visitors, rather than all surrounding seawater.
figurative.accept: The ship is submerged in ordinary seawater but outside the carrying field, so unloading remains safe.

figurative.stands_for: The channel bank in the Twilight. In the Scald, Grey and Chill it means reachable working ground beyond the hull.
figurative.accept: On the Scald the crew steps off the hull onto hot mineral ground and reaches a mat patch by an ordinary walking path, with no channel or literal bank in sight.

accept: On the Twilight floor the crew unloads, works on the channel bank, returns to the hull and flies away.
A low-skill crew can stay on the hull and choose a bank route while a current remains hazardous elsewhere.
On the Scald the crew steps off the hull onto hot mineral ground and reaches a mat patch by an ordinary walking path, with no channel or literal bank in sight.
reject: The crew spawns beside a hatch while its ship remains elsewhere, or returns by a pawn menu.
The ship lands astride a live channel and unloading automatically carries the crew toward the sink.
bars.lazy: none: The sentence names the contrasted player outcome; each plausible shortcut below contradicts an explicit clause, rather than satisfying it.

range.varies: All 4 named seas; existing fixed-world tiles represented by disposable authored floor fixtures, not new planets. Map sizes 150, 250, 325 and 400 cells square; 4 ship rotations, hulls of bounding width 9, 25 and 49 cells, edge/corner/central landing candidates; empty/loaded cargo, 1/8/40 colonists, intact and interrupted unloading; arrival, departure, re-entry and reload. Sweep boundary placements in geometry model, not just these samples. On the Scald floor the route from the hull to working ground uses ordinary hot substrate with no boiling-contact terrain. The cool margin is beach-only. Include standard departure with the floor kept, simulation time away and return with or without a save/reload while away.
range.left_out: No worldgen, alternative worlds, individual diving or surface settlement. A broken grav engine from combat is vanilla failure, not guaranteed rescue by this mod.

sees.instrument: T40 situation/state adapter plus T41 landing/field geometry export; inspect real landing reservations, floor parent/layer, reachable paths and ordinary launch result.
sees.start: A supplied save with a functional occupied gravship and a legal sea-floor destination; no hatch; actual landing footprint, current field, map identity and payload recorded before entry.
sees.on: All kept mechanics at shipped defaults; all DLC; no research/dev lock; next-version extras off; actual composed Baroque Biomes dependencies present. Never force the sky clear, suppress animals, disable growth, or replace real current with a staged dummy. Differential controls run in separate copies and do not count as the passing observation.
sees.control: An empty test map could allow any ship. Require an active channel elsewhere on Twilight and record zero intersection with its reserved landing footprint. Exercise ordinary launch and payload readback; a getter saying launch-allowed alone cannot prove travel. On ordinary return, match the retained parent, map and an untouched fixture placed before launch. A regenerated floor with the right biome would fail this read.
sees.reset: Use disposable copies of an existing fixed-world save and its local floor maps; restore that copy and settings snapshot after reading. Never modify the canonical world or reroll a planet.
sees.live_only_why: Not live-only: state/geometry evidence can decide these outcomes once its adapter agrees with real game transitions; an uncalibrated model never passes a bar.

meant.intent: These are distinct places, not renamed vanilla water; each land picture is the indispensable content of the bundle.
meant.source: delegated synthesis of the_scald.md artistic theme, the_twilight_deep.md artistic theme, the_grey_deep.md mineral floor additions and the_propane_lake_floor_sitting_agenda_2026-10-02.md; no new owner aesthetic approval claimed.

figurative.stands_for: Amber shafts of light, not solid gold pillars.
figurative.accept: A warm amber shaft illuminating plants, with no mineable metal column, reads as Twilight.

figurative.stands_for: The living translucent waveglass organism overhead, not a constructed glass roof.
figurative.accept: An irregular veined translucent organism with pale skylight rims forms the ceiling; there are no glass roof tiles.

accept: At normal colony zoom, cyan water and rainbow mats identify the Scald, gold-lit gardens beneath waveglass identify the Twilight, pale mineral forms stay readable as distinct silhouettes through the Grey’s murk, and dark fuel pools stand out against the Chill’s ice floor.
In the Grey, a mineral-rich scene still leaves distinct pools and silhouettes rather than a white screen; the Twilight has dark ground between light columns.
The living giant moves far overhead beneath the waveglass and is distinguishable from a well marker or static roof ornament.
reject: The sea names change but the floor scenes are interchangeable blue water with recoloured fog.
A solid opaque overlay hides pawns, current boundaries or the only bank route.
A gardener label or fixed roof ornament replaces the giant animal in the ordinary play view.

Native fauna die thirsty beside their own water, or vanish when moving between states.

bars.says: On the Scald beach, boiling water gives an unprotected visitor both contact burns and hot-spring comfort, the cooler margin offers comfortable bathing without burns, and neither water is drinkable.

meant.intent: The frozen Scald sheet makes the same water hurt and comfort a visitor. The cooler beach margin keeps the bathing contrast and shares the body-water drinking ban. Native life remains the environmental exception.
meant.source: the_scald.md Always true, hard bans 1 and 3 and §§7–8; HotSpring in RM_ScaldWater.xml and RM_ScaldMargin.xml; delegated beach-layer placement from the floor’s mere heat in §4.

figurative.stands_for: Odyssey’s ordinary HotSpring mood memory from traversal or bathing, with the margin also eligible for normal recreation. It implies no treatment of injuries.
figurative.accept: A visitor has a new pleasant HotSpring memory from the same crossing that left a burn needing care.

accept: An unprotected beach visitor crossing the boil gains a hot-spring mood thought and takes a contact burn from the same water.
At the cooler margin a visitor bathes comfortably without further contact burns, then returns to dry shore and drinks from supplies brought ashore.
reject: The boil deals a contact burn but provides no hot-spring comfort, or it awards comfort while an unprotected crossing costs no injury.
The cooler bathing margin burns the bather or gives no bathing comfort.
Boiling water or the cooler margin supplies a drinking job.
bars.lazy: none: The sentence requires both simultaneous outcomes from the boil, the margin’s comfort without contact burns, and drinking denial on both.

range.varies: On the neighbouring beach, compare RM_ScaldWaterDeep, RM_ScaldWaterOceanDeep, RM_ScaldWaterMovingChestDeep, RM_ScaldWaterShallow, RM_ScaldWaterOceanShallow and RM_ScaldWaterMovingShallow via the resolved terrain/liquid bindings. Use supported normal visitor crossings and separate burn-eligible entry routes for any variants that ordinary pathing will not choose. Compare dry shore, cooler RM_ScaldMargin, repeat crossings, ordinary bathing, steam/still weather and reload. The burn/comfort contrast uses mood-capable unprotected visitors; use protected visitors and natives as controls where eligible. Hold ambient air and solar geometry equal for matched comparisons.
range.left_out: The submerged floor has ambient heat only and is outside this beach-contact bar. HotSpring is an ordinary mood effect. Protection, natives and pawns without mood follow their existing physiology or capability. Steam purity and solar implementation stay in rules/checks. No medical benefit or new bathing job belongs to this bar.

sees.instrument: T40 and T45 record actual jobs, terrain, damage causes, HotSpring mood memories, bathing recreation and attempted drinking. M4 replays the resolved beach mechanism and checks it against those state reads.
sees.start: Real Scald beach with resolved boiling terrain, dry approach and accessible cooler margin. Choose healthy, mood-capable visitors with known protection and no pre-existing HotSpring memory. Record starting temperature, sun geometry, health, mood, recreation and water source.

Require new contact damage and a new HotSpring memory attributed to the same boiling traversal, then ordinary bathing and comfort with no new contact damage on the margin. Read actual job and ingestion outcomes for each liquid. In separate controls remove the HotSpring binding, remove contact damage, or make the margin potable. A terrain description, lingering unrelated mood memory or ambient heat alone cannot pass.

bars.says: A Twilight harvester can gather visibly more forage from the productive bank than from the floor’s other gathering ground, including the off-bank lit gardens, and read the current boundary, but entering carrying water moves an unsecured visitor toward the sink, and an announced undersurge brings that boundary onto the bank.

meant.intent: The signature joins temptation, legible boundary, carry and changing reach; an invisible harmless river or an unavoidable unloading trap both fail it.
meant.source: the_twilight_deep.md §§3 and 7, underwater rivers and richest gathering ground, and the no-swimmable-river hard ban; delegated safe working edge from the current and readable-sign ruling.

figurative.stands_for: The best reachable natural gathering ground in ordinary play, judged by visible harvestable plants and successful gathering against the floor’s other forage ground, including lit gardens away from the current.
figurative.accept: The bank offers a better ordinary harvest even than a lit garden away from the current, though the garden’s soil is as fertile for planted crops.

figurative.stands_for: Recognise bed shape and stakes against bank ground in play, not see a separate coloured liquid.
figurative.accept: The moving water itself is invisible, yet the dry-looking trough and outer stake line let a visitor pick the bank route.

figurative.stands_for: The dense current within the authoritative channel field, not the entire submerged map.
figurative.accept: A visitor can work submerged on a bank outside the carrying field without drifting.

figurative.stands_for: The current’s terminal basin where a victim remains findable and rescuable, not deletion or necessarily a visible hole.
figurative.accept: A victim lies marked Sunk in a shallow-looking mud basin; no hole opens and no pawn vanishes.

accept: The bank offers visibly more forage than the reachable open-floor patches, including the lit gardens away from the current. A worker gathers there under ordinary orders, sees the bed and stakes, and can withdraw after a surge warning and resume later.
A visitor entering the channel is interrupted and carried downstream; a harness or existing arrest works helps manage exposure without turning the centre into a swimming route.
reject: A bank grow-soil stat is higher but harvesters see and gather no more forage there than on comparable open floor, so the bank offers no reason to work near the current.
The bank beats matched dim floor, but lit gardens away from the current offer as much or more, so workers with ordinary orders gather there and never choose the bank.
The terrain looks like harmless mud, the worker receives no warning, and movement to the sink is the first sign.
A warning fires but the dry-looking bed is indistinguishable from bank silt, or the visible stake line misidentifies the widened reach.
A pawn repeatedly walks through the centre faster than registration and never experiences carry.
Current arrows move items while an ordinary colonist crosses safely, or the surge occupies the ship’s sole usable exit and all safe banks.
bars.lazy: none: The explicit comparison includes the lit gardens away from the current and requires visibly more forage and successful gathering. A fertility number, decorative growth or an advantage over dim ground alone fails it.

range.varies: Full authored Twilight fields at map sizes 150/250/325/400, all 8 bearings, straight/diagonal/overlap/eddy/sink/edge placements and generated obstruction patterns; first entry and repeated crossings, calm/surge/start/end, naked/harnessed, normal/downed, native/nonnative, haulables, walls/doors/ford/weir, no/8/40 colonists. Sweep registration phase 0..249 ticks and process phase 0..14, settings pace extrema, reload just before due movement, and both forage-before-haul and haul-before-forage order. Visual boundary sort covers ordinary zoom and map-wide views, dim ground versus gold columns, sparse and grown native clutter, calm, announced onset and expanded surge; not just a selected or debug-outlined channel. Compare reachable bank patches with the strongest reachable off-bank forage alternatives in each ordinary floor view, including lit gardens away from the current. Compare similar patch areas and harvest histories with each patch’s actual light and ordinary routes. Sample fresh native seeding, mature growth and regrowth after comparable pressure. Include dim banks competing with lit gardens and banks under columns. Treat a recently cleared patch as depletion and test recovery over the declared cycle.
range.left_out: No cargo-float logistics, no guaranteed rescue from choosing to enter the centre, no new FlowWorks fertility/weir engine. Ordinary bank harvest does not promise to feed an arbitrarily large colony indefinitely. No silt-trap or worked-silt dependency.

sees.instrument: M2 geometry and timing sweep plus T40 adapter trace of actual cell entry, current membership, displacement, job interruption, warning delivery and bank route. Kernel selftests are inputs, not a substitute for engine movement/reachability. Boundary legibility additionally requires a live look: a cold reader sorts unlabelled ordinary play views of dry-looking beds, bank silt and surge stakes, marking carrying-bed and outer stake-line boundaries before seeing T40 field overlays. Compare those marked regions to the exported calm/surge reach; a warning event alone cannot pass the visual clause. Use the same ordinary views to compare bank forage with reachable alternatives, including off-bank lit gardens. T40 and T42 export reachable harvestable plants, available harvest products and completed gather jobs by patch.
sees.start: Generated full field with real bed/bank presentation, forage plants, an ordinary visitor path across and along it, actual ship reservation, no forced pawn teleport into the sink.
sees.on: All kept mechanics at shipped defaults; all DLC; no research/dev lock; next-version extras off; actual composed Baroque Biomes dependencies present. Never force the sky clear, suppress animals, disable growth, or replace real current with a staged dummy. Differential controls run in separate copies and do not count as the passing observation.
sees.control: A scripted teleport could look like current. Record pre-move field, due time, movement call and interrupted job; separate no-flow and blocked-edge controls must prevent the displacement. Verify bank forage completes while native growth and wildlife are running. For the visual sort hide selection labels, arrows and debug fields; include negative controls with bed art blended into bank silt and displaced stakes. A reader must reject those even when the warning fires. Sample calm, surge onset and full surge views with the same lighting and native clutter as the passing views. With silt works off, keep both the bank and off-bank forage reachable under ordinary orders without a bank-only zone or hand-picked target. Record path lengths, recent harvest and the actual light at each patch. Require a visibly better harvest even against the lit off-bank option and record completed bank gathering. In separate matched-light copies, neutralize the R15 weight while holding terrain fertility and visible weircomb fixed to isolate the natural placement effect.
sees.reset: Use disposable copies of an existing fixed-world save and its local floor maps; restore that copy and settings snapshot after reading. Never modify the canonical world or reroll a planet.
sees.live_only_why: The carrying liquid looks like the surrounding water. State can prove bed/stake placement and warning delivery, but only the ordinary play view can show whether a cold reader distinguishes the dry-looking channel and stake line from harmless bank silt. Calibrated state and geometry still decide movement, timing and route access.

meant.intent: A fair consequence follows the current and preserves the no-unreadable-vanishing ruling; movement into a sink is not silent despawning.
meant.source: Standing no animal or pawn vanishes without readable sign; current source default Recoverable and Sunk comp; delegated rescue predicate tightened beyond the source’s generic roof check.

figurative.accept: A marked victim remains findable on the basin floor without disappearing down a hole.

accept: The carried colonist is placed at a reachable basin location, marked sunk and worsening; a rescuer removes them from carrying water into safe shelter or a safe carrier and the condition starts improving.
A dead or interrupted rescuer leaves a findable victim or corpse; transferring the victim aboard the ship does not keep applying an off-map death ramp.
reject: The pawn is deleted at the sink, or only a log line mentions a missing colonist.
A roof placed over a live sink counts as rescue while the pawn is still in carrying water.
A full sink deposits the victim outside the basin through a wall, repeats the arrival endlessly, or loses the victim on reload.

bars.says: A Twilight visitor sees a living protected giant gardener beneath the waveglass and can inspect temporary gold light columns that age across visits, go dark at expiry and are replaced on eligible garden ground.

meant.intent: The living lid always has its protected animal, and its temporary light migrates through the native garden. The animal’s continued presence and the natural well lifecycle carry those two land promises.
meant.source: the_twilight_deep.md §§3-6, ratified 2026-09-07 and waveglass amendment 2026-09-26; delegated protected-creature boundary for this version, not an owner ruling of immortality.

figurative.stands_for: Warm amber light shafts, not solid gold objects.
figurative.accept: Plants grow in an amber shaft of light without any metal pillar to mine.

accept: A living giant swims far overhead beneath the waveglass. The same individual is still there after departure, reload and return.
The crew inspects a column, works in its garden, then returns after time away to the same still-active column with less time remaining.
A waning column reaches the end of its lifetime and goes dark. A new column opens on eligible ground on the ordinary schedule.
reject: The waveglass remains with a label, a static ornament or a floor-walking animal in place of its living overhead swimmer.
The gardener can be killed or removed while the waveglass remains. A death followed by respawn leaves the same gap.

A gold well acts as a permanent lamp: its countdown freezes while the floor ages, or it reaches expiry and keeps shining. The garden also fails if eligible ground stays dark when a replacement is due.
bars.lazy: none: The sentence names the contrasted player outcome; each plausible shortcut below contradicts an explicit clause, rather than satisfying it.

range.varies: RM-only and campaign-enhanced loads with next-version extras off. First arrival, continuing and retained floors, including reload while away and return. Record the living gardener across applicable harm and removal paths. Cover isolated and overlapping wells in opening, standing and waning stages, expiry and replacement, and a pending replacement with eligible ground absent then restored. Include occupied and retained-away ticking, dim and gold-lit sites, current and ship exclusions, 150..400-square maps and 0/8/40 colonists. Keep the R7 years-scale default.
range.left_out: Campaign habitation, pane impacts, lid-dark, suulk, interactive ceiling routing, rim jobs and a killable-gardener or roof-collapse scenario are deferred. Protection is a delegated version limit. Explicitly abandoned floors and opted-out sandbox floors are outside the retention promise.

sees.instrument: T40 reads the actual saved gardener identity and life state and records well clocks, lifecycle dispatch, LightLedger contributions and Scribe transitions. T43 supplies the overhead animal read and B2 judges its ordinary presentation. T46 records the live expiry and replacement branch for this bar independently of the K11 regression result.
sees.start: Begin with a normally initialized Twilight floor at defaults. Record its living gardener, map and well ids, remaining life and effective light. Trace the same gardener and active well during occupancy, ordinary absence and an actual Scribe reload while away. Use a second copy for the expiry and replacement reading: staged start state, normal update path. Initialize an otherwise valid waning well just before expiry, with reachable eligible ground for replacement. Run ordinary map ticks from there through closure and scheduled replacement. In a separate branch block eligible ground, let the replacement become due, then restore eligibility and let normal dispatch complete it.
sees.on: All kept mechanics at shipped defaults; all DLC; no research/dev lock; next-version extras off; actual composed Baroque Biomes dependencies present. Never force the sky clear, suppress animals, disable growth, or replace real current with a staged dummy. Differential controls run in separate copies and do not count as the passing observation.
sees.control: Read the same living gardener across attempts at harm or removal and through reload. A static label or replacement individual fails. Compare the countdown with age, lifespan and elapsed map ticks. At expiry require the expired id to lose its LightLedger contribution while any overlapping neighbour remains lit. Require normal dispatch to open a fresh id with its own light on eligible ground, and to retain a pending replacement while ground is blocked. A countdown-only control that leaves the old glow active or suppresses the due replacement must fail. From the staged start, use ordinary ticks and site eligibility with every kept mechanic on. Leave forced advance callbacks and deferred gardener jobs off.
sees.reset: Use disposable copies of an existing fixed-world save and its local floor maps; restore that copy and settings snapshot after reading. Never modify the canonical world or reroll a planet.
sees.live_only_why: T40/T43/T46 can decide the persistence, protection, closure and replacement clauses from actual game state and lifecycle transitions. B2 separately judges the ordinary view of the animal and light columns.

tests.reject: The living lid always has its protected animal, and its temporary light migrates through the native garden. The animal’s continued presence and the natural well lifecycle carry those two land promises.
tests.renormalize: The outcome survives retuning yields, durations, sizes and art variants. Ranges exercise changed values without locking them into the experience.
tests.first_version: Land, life or the current signature, or a named necessary adapter; see census and definition.

bars.says: Through a full-map season of sea visits, foraging, bank work, rescue and return travel, the crew keeps recognising each habitat and finding native life, with reachable Twilight gardens under aging wells and ordinary foragers choosing the banks in calm as the current alternates between work and warned danger without a flood of hazards, an emptied floor, stalled travel or recurring errors.

meant.intent: The complete default version must remain recognisable and workable together; isolated proofs cannot hide a map-scale collapse or a reload/order defect.
meant.source: delegated whole-version inference from owner’s 2026-11-16 cleansing brief and the kept promises; qualitative experience, not a mandated numerical equilibrium.

figurative.stands_for: Repeated hazards remove the usable visit route, whether or not any liquid level rises.
figurative.accept: An undersurge reaches a garden edge but the ship and a bank route stay usable; this is danger without a flood of hazards.

figurative.stands_for: The loss of viable native life and its food chain, not an obligation to preserve each initial animal.
figurative.accept: Predation reduces the shoal while surviving prey still feed predators and replace losses; the floor is not emptied.

figurative.stands_for: Ordinary arrival, return or required task transitions stop completing under normal conditions, not a crew choosing to wait.
figurative.accept: A crew waits out a warned surge then completes its bank work and return flight; that delay is not stalled travel.

accept: Under ordinary orders, the expedition’s foragers choose the richer Twilight banks during calm while lit gardens away from the current remain available. The expedition harvests among native life, responds to an undersurge, recovers a victim and returns by ship. After saving and loading during the visit, the crew still finds a reachable Twilight garden beneath the columns with less time left on the well.
Reversing whether the crew hauls or forages first changes the story without turning the banks into a continuous unavoidable sink or erasing the food chain.
reject: Each isolated scene works, but combined growth hides every bank, predators erase the catch population, or the working Twilight floor has no reachable garden light, or ordinary workers gather only in the off-bank lit gardens because the banks offer no better harvest.
The sky is locked clear, wildlife is suppressed or current is disabled for the season recording.
Reload duplicates carrying victims or weather, a different action order blocks the ship, or repeated errors replace ordinary play.
bars.lazy: none: The sentence names the contrasted player outcome; each plausible shortcut below contradicts an explicit clause, rather than satisfying it.

range.varies: Each of the 4 seas runs on a full 250-square floor for 15 game days at shipped defaults, with 150/325/400-square boundary coverage through M1/M2; test 1,8,40 colonists, native wildlife and ordinary predation/growth, real weather/atmosphere, current, wells, ordinary salvage and all kept dependency features. Include new arrival and day-100 continued-save regimes, mid-season Scribe save/reload, and matched copies reversing harvest/haul/shelter/rescue order. Twilight covers calm, surge, return to the retained floor, reachable gardens, a living overhead gardener, ordinary bank foraging in calm with off-bank lit forage available, and wells aging at the R7 years-scale default. Continue until a natural surge occurs if the season did not contain one. A naturally occurring light-stage transition can be recorded if it falls inside the trace. B7 reads expiry and replacement in a separate start state. Time compression may skip rendering only: preserve all simulation ticks, RNG ordering, jobs, pathing, weather, temperature, plant/pawn ticks, hunger/thirst, movement, due times and save boundaries.
range.left_out: Next-version extras are off. No alternative planets, cosmetic variant quotas, universal food self-sufficiency or guaranteed survival of deliberately abandoned visitors. No requirement for well replacement inside the season. Leave well ages and lifetimes unedited throughout the whole trace.

sees.instrument: T42 whole-mod recorder and M3 calibrated whole-system model, anchored by real full-map traces; T40 checks ordinary action completion, native persistence, current reachability and reload. B2 separately judges presentation. A model with invented ecology or inactive dependencies cannot certify this bar.
sees.start: A clean disposable fixed-world save with real full maps, healthy equipped expedition, native populations, a functional ship, all kept systems enabled and research available; configuration fingerprint and every gate recorded. Record baseline counts, causes and geometry before advancing.
sees.on: All kept mechanics at shipped defaults; all DLC; no research/dev lock; next-version extras off; actual composed Baroque Biomes dependencies present. Never force the sky clear, suppress animals, disable growth, or replace real current with a staged dummy. Differential controls run in separate copies and do not count as the passing observation.
sees.control: A large scene can appear stable because actors cannot act or time barely advanced. Require completed ordinary jobs, genuine births/growth/feeding/drinking/death/remains events where relevant, actual elapsed game ticks, effective gates, naturally initiated current transitions, and stable well ids with finite countdowns advancing with elapsed map ticks alongside the living gardener and usable garden routes. Record which patches ordinary foragers choose in calm and verify that lit off-bank forage was reachable without restricting work to the bank. Compare recorded event/state budgets to the calibrated model and use withheld action-order/reload traces; clean logs alone cannot pass.
sees.reset: Use disposable copies of an existing fixed-world save and its local floor maps; restore that copy and settings snapshot after reading. Never modify the canonical world or reroll a planet.
sees.live_only_why: Not live-only: state/geometry evidence can decide these outcomes once its adapter agrees with real game transitions; an uncalibrated model never passes a bar.

checks.what: Parse effective XML rosters by child node names and resolved patches; record positive animalDensity and complete fishable-to-living pairing. Existing validation.py is partial coverage, not proof of encounters. Read resolved grouping intent against the actual initial and refill paths. A group-size def alone cannot establish a school.
Record declared current widths/cadences, scan/process intervals, sink flags and enum defaults; existing Kernel/RM_ChannelKernel.cs and SelfTest/TerminalBiomesFuzz.cs checks stay regression-only.
Audit field/terrain correspondence and actual ship reservation, dimensions, setting extrema, corrupt/partial grids and cycles; no live field silently lacks a readable bed.
Check all settings missing-value defaults, actual consumers, Scribe round-trip and composed-package registrations. Each deferred feature has an effective false default and no default availability.
Check native temperature, water, light, food and flight bindings against actual resolved defs, including growth temperature curves and industrial nonfood flags. No species-name sampling.

Check layer-specific weather bindings, no rain/thunder/water snow underwater, Scald margin nonpotability, no local sun fields; existing sea-floor text/no-rain scripts are partial regressions. Check that steam adds no poisoning/fouling effect or private steam-health currency; these are implementation constraints, not a separate experience bar.
Check Scribe identity, holder contents, terminal sink arrival, rescue status and LightLedger restoration at each save boundary; mutation controls must fail.

Record count/time budgets for growth, population, current exposure, safe route availability and errors over full-map traces; tune against qualitative bars, never promote a numeric budget into refusal. Keep harvestable counts and job outcomes for banks and off-bank lit gardens under actual light. Keep matched-light counts as a diagnostic control.
Audit declared hard dependencies and assembly/def references in composed packaging; About.xml standalone prose is historical and must not decide current world or load behaviour.

Retain review findings only after source confirmation: current map-ownership and sink-idempotence fixes, cadence due-time preservation, graze persistence and off-map Sunk recovery are already visible in source. Do not reopen them from old review prose.

M1 stages records just before opening, waning, closure and replacement due time at the R7 years-scale default, then lets the normal update path cross each boundary. Check clock and light updates, persistence of a pending replacement without an eligible site, and opening on eligible ground when a site becomes available. Check fresh and migrated lifetimes, setting defaults and preservation of saved stage and identity. Starting tuning target is two to four in-game years for a new well. Cross-check ordinary elapsed-age dispatch against T42 and use a naturally aged save for unstaged boundary corroboration when available. Record this regression sweep as a check. B7 separately specifies its own staged start and ordinary-update observation of expiry and replacement.

rules.rule: Preserve one fixed world and the sea-floor layer; no new worldgen, surface settlement or hatch route. Ship reservations and its bank access are excluded from authored current and surge reach.

Current field is authoritative for carrying and siting exclusions. Terrain must show its boundary, but replacing terrain cannot secretly erase or create carry. A generated obstruction cannot leave a live downstream path through walls.

Use the existing ChannelKernel cadence comparisons: centre stronger than margin, surge stronger than calm, harness caps carry without immunity. Exact numeric cadences remain checks. Remove the legacy slow-registration option from supported default behaviour.

Default sink outcome is Recoverable. Sink arrival is terminal and idempotent; no source-map movement after transfer. Rescue requires leaving the dangerous liquid for safe shelter or safe carriage; a roof over the sink is insufficient. Never choose an unchecked fallback cell.

Take Direct Sun only from shared geometry into vanilla felt temperature. Steam/hot fog use ordinary air temperature, Scald contact is the shared liquid injury path; natives drink their environmental liquid. No local solar offset or steam health currency.

Separate Scald beach steam sky from calm submerged bubbles. Grey salt snow is falling crystals. On the Scald beach, shared contact damage and ordinary HotSpring mood apply to the boiling terrain. Beach-only RM_ScaldMargin permits ordinary comfort and bathing without burns. Both are nonpotable. Replace the floor’s hot-liquid bands with walkable mineral RM_ScaldFloorSubstrate at ordinary ambient heat, carrying over the existing native mat habitat. Keep vent shapes and bubbles as presentation without boiling pools.

Keep natural well lifecycle and gold glow. At shipped defaults each well has a finite years-scale lifetime, following the Twilight sheet’s hard ban and migrating light over time. Use actual current membership for sites and LightLedger for composed glow. At expiry remove that well’s active light and queue ordinary replacement on eligible ground. Leave rim work, tenancy, graze pressure, event-dependent flora, culture and the forced advance callback with their deferred extras. K11 stages lifecycle boundaries through the same update path. Preserve saved identities and migrate legacy week-clock records without resetting their stage or creating new wells at load.

Retain ordinary roster entries and their habitat/food/light needs. Shared native physiology and movement are not opt-in extras; no eviction or fictional flyer grounded by def omission. Ordinary static plant glow does not need charge/wilt behaviour. Keep Grey wild arrivals single and Twilight shore solitary. Below the Twilight lid, initial floor seeding and replenishment must produce the declared niim and noolim shoals in their lit and dim habitats respectively. Use ordinary group spawning and movement where supported through the existing fauna seam.

Preserve defs and saved holders when switching features off. Gate dispatch, running jobs, availability and reload reassertion. Master/per-sea/per-major-feature settings explain effective state; existing cross-biome controls stay off and unsupported.

All kept dependency mechanics run together during evidence collection, at shipped defaults and with all DLC. Modelling changes neither the game’s population density nor its time order to obtain a pass.

Use DivingInteraction’s ordinary retainable seabed site. At shipped defaults a standard gravship visit keeps the floor map ticking when the ship leaves, even with no player pawns there. A return to that retained site reuses the same map, ecology, gardener and well ledger. The ledger advances on ordinary map ticks during the absence; a save/load preserves elapsed age and does not advance time while the simulation is paused. Explicit vanilla discard or abandonment ends that floor; a legal subsequent landing there generates a new floor with its own occupants and ledger. Do not add a parallel retention ledger or claim a preserved floor after discard.

On Twilight floors, use a local natural-spawn weight for RM_Gloamurn and RM_HoolimbrePlant at initial seeding and ordinary wild-plant replenishment. Multiply the selection weight of each eligible cell–species pair for those two plants when the cell is both in the authoritative bank and tagged RM_BankSilt. Keep the ordinary weight elsewhere. Apply the ordinary species habitat, light, occupancy and spacing checks before weighting, and preserve walkable routes and ordinary harvest products. Leave crop fertility unchanged. C10 supplies the existing plants, C22 the bank and C30 the missing spawn bias. Keep static bank weircomb as habitat dressing. T50 keeps worked-silt conversion off by default.

meetings.why: DivingInteraction supplies a retainable RM_SeabedSite MapParent (canBePlayerHome and vanilla Abandon comp) and selects the generator for a fresh floor. On a retained ticking map WellLedger.ExposeData preserves records, and MapComponentTick advances the active wells without an occupancy gate. Ordinary retention and aging therefore agree under R14. The remaining unknown is whether real hull reservations and pathing leave a safe launch, bank and rescue corridor once the hatch-only exclusion is removed. M2 tests that geometry; M1/T40 confirms the composed runtime really keeps and ticks the chosen site across departure, reload while away and re-entry.
Carry, harvest, site selection, sink/rescue and ship reservation touch the same cells. Straight spokes, crossings, walls and missed entry phases may destroy the safe operating region.

Transfer, hediffs, wells, off-state callbacks and holders can agree pairwise yet duplicate or strand an entity across a reload. Kernel serialization is not Scribe proof. The same protected gardener and the well ledger must survive a retained-map visit and save/reload without a duplicate or a death hidden by respawn.

A gate removes behaviour/availability, never defs or the return route. Separate ordinary roster bodies from their attached extras; retained helpers consume no deferred products. This is an architectural argument, not a claim all current gates implement it.

Beach steam and submerged bubbles occupy separate maps. Twilight uses bed shape/stakes rather than visible liquid colour, and the far-overhead swimmer shares no floor occupancy or pathing. Grey mineral crowding permits solitary fauna. These spatial roles have no logical conflict; final legibility is explicitly judged by B2/B5, not claimed from the argument.

Native growth, catch replacement, predation, water eligibility, harvest and moving light jointly set whether a floor stays alive. A season with every kept mechanism active has not been recorded here. Initial seeding and refill may produce different grouping, and decorative silt growth can hide a lack of harvestable bank plants. Test real spawn episodes, spacing and reachable regrowth.

Well turnover, current avoidance and native growth could leave a working floor without reachable lit gardens. M5 checks light loss at expiry, ordinary replacement and site eligibility with the current and growth active. R14 keeps the ordinary tick path active after departure. The same ledger and living protected gardener must survive a return.

Match ambient heat and solar geometry to test hot-spring comfort and contact effects separately from the floor’s ambient heat. Existing dependency sources show their seams, while actual delivery and job outcomes still require M4.

A full current book, reachable forage, light site search and all native actors may stall a large colony despite correct isolated kernels.
